newsitem.title: UK: UK medics say tobacco firms should pay health costs.
newsitem.headline: UK medics say tobacco firms should pay health costs.

text.p: The British Medical Association (BMA) on Saturday urged health authorities to try to recover from tobacco companies some of the millions of pounds of public money spent every year on treating smoking-related diseases.

The BMA -- which represents doctors and health workers throughout the country -- said it believed that tobacco companies in Britain should be brought to account following a landmark $368.5 billion settlement in the United States.
"Our message to health trusts is to look at all possibilities for holding the tobacco industry accountable for the cost of health care," said Bill O'Neill, scientific and health officer for the BMA.
"The tobacco companies should be getting very worried. At last there is a concerted attack on them now, particularly with a new government considering a ban on advertising," O'Neil added.
O'Neill said Britain spent 610 million pounds ($1 billion) a year on health care for smoking related diseases.
However British tobacco companies said they had no intention of following the U.S. lead.

Britain's largest cigarette maker Gallaher, which was hived off from American Brands and floated on the London stock market last month, said it would be unaffected by the settlement and would fight any similar attempt at litigation in Britain.

"We have complete confidence in the law and judicial process in the U.K. and we are not guided by the development in the U.S.," said a spokesman for Gallaher, whose brands include Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut.

The first British test case to be brought by lung cancer victims is expected to reach the courts next month. A group of 47 people are claiming damages against Gallaher and Imperial Tobacco and lawyers say a judgment in their favour could lead to a $1 billion annual bill for the industry.

"We call on the British tobacco companies to consider adopting the same settlement proposals as those of their American counterparts without the need for claims to be taken through the courts," said lawyer Martyn Day. ($ = 0.603 British Pounds)
